title: Evaluating Temporal Resolution Limitations by Exploiting Latest Developments in Detector Hardware and AI-based Denoising Algorithm in Application to Environmental TEM
content: Environmental Transmission Electron Microscopy (ETEM) is an indispensable tool for studying nanomaterials and catalysts in gaseous environments. The technique enables investigation of various processes in solids including diffusion, phase transformations, crystal growth, corrosion, and catalytic reactions. With current state-of-the-art sensors designed for TEM, the typical temporal resolution is in millisecond range for sensors larger than 512x512 pixels. However, this resolution is often insufficient to capture dynamic processes in solids for which timescales can vary from femtoseconds to hours.
